subject: Supplier onboarding: identity confirmation and payment-path decision
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-26T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Supplier onboarding: identity confirmation and payment-path decision

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through the demo and the proposed integration pattern. Quick recap and three asks so we can move procurement along: 

1) Commercial path preference: please confirm whether Acme prefers (a) PO + Net30 (preferred by finance), (b) corporate card, or (c) AWS Marketplace (we can enable marketplace billing but it requires additional enrollment).

2) Vendor identity & tax form: you mentioned Acme is a US entity. Can you confirm if we should expect a W-9? If a W-8 is required instead, tell us the entity type and country.

3) Banking / remit instructions: if you route via invoices/POs, we need bank remit details or portal enrollment steps. If you want marketplace billing, let us know and I’ll share the enablement checklist.

Next steps we propose: once you confirm (1) + (2), I’ll share our vendor packet (attached) and route a DocuSign for the legal/finance contact. If PO path is chosen, Ben on my team will work with your AP to finalize the W-9 and bank validation.

Attachments: Redwood_Vendor_Packet_v2.pdf (see vendor onboarding checklist, required fields list)
Link: https://docs.google.com/drive/folders/0AexampleVendorPacket
HubSpot: HS-129034

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation so we can keep the March/April timeline.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acmehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-26T19:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Supplier onboarding: identity confirmation and payment-path decision

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the recap. A few quick answers and requests: 

• Commercial path: Acme will go PO + Net30 for initial pilots. We standardize on PO for new SaaS vendors.
• Tax form: We need a completed W-9 from Redwood (Acme requires tax name + EIN on file).
• Banking instructions: Please provide the bank remit details (ACH + wire instructions) or, if available, a vendor portal enrollment link so AP can onboard Redwood directly.

Two asks from my side: can you pre-populate the W-9 with Redwood’s legal name and EIN so our intake team can accept it, and include an invoice template matching your suggested PO number placement? Also confirm whether Redwood supports billing via AWS Marketplace (we may evaluate that later but want to know if it’s an option).

If you send the W-9 + remit info today, I’ll route to our AP and aim to issue a PO by the end of next week.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Myers
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health
jordan.myers@acmehealth.com
Phone: (212) 555-0199

Thanks for the quick reply and the confirmation on PO + Net30. See answers and enclosed materials below. 

Summary / attachments I’m sending now:

• Banking instructions workbook (ACH + wire remits, sample invoice template) — Attachment: Banking_Instructions.xlsx

Checklist for Acme AP to accept vendor: 
- Confirm Redwood legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- EIN: 12-3456789 (on attached W-9)
- Primary remit method: ACH (details in Banking_Instructions.xlsx)
- Invoice requirements: include PO number on header, net 30 terms, contact: ap@redwood.ai

Marketplace note: we do support AWS Marketplace billing, but that enrollment is separate from our standard vendor setup and can add ~2–3 weeks to activation. For your pilot we recommend PO path to speed time-to-invoice. If you’d like marketplace as fallback we can start the enablement concurrently.

Next steps I’ll own: route DocuSign for signature where needed and confirm billing contact. Ben, can you pick up bank validation once Jordan confirms receipt?
